To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

tree-hole mosquitoes are organized into drought-prone and -resistant communities, that these communities have distinct ecological requirements, and that drought affects the survivorship of the drought-prone species by the direct action on larvae and pupae by dehydration, and by the indirect action of predation.
the duration, frequency and timing of drought affect the survivorship, distribution, and abundance of tree-hole mosquitoes in North Florida, USA.
the duration, frequency and timing of drought affect the survivorship and community organization of pre-adult mosquitoes in tree holes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of drought in the organization of tree hole mosquito communities.
the organization of tree hole mosquito communities.
how tree hole mosquitoes organize into communities that vary with the frequency of drought and with how these communities vary in their ability to persist through drought.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
drought affects tree-hole mosquito communities by the direct action and indirect modulation of predator activity, but that these effects are not easily predicted by tree-hole stability.
drought affects tree hole mosquito communities by altering the physical and chemical properties of tree holes.
the physical and chemical attributes that mosquitoes cue on to select oviposition sites are not good indicators of the likelihood of a hole remaining filled and available to the mosquito larvae.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

drought affects mosquito communities by differentially affecting the survival of drought-sensitive species, and by affecting the survival of these species in a manner that is independent of their host trees.
the physical and chemical attributes that affect tree-hole stability also affect the organization of tree hole mosquito communities.
the drought-prone tree-hole mosquito community is more organized than the drought-resistant community.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the community structure of mosquitoes in tree holes reflects a trade-off between the benefits of drought resistance and the costs of increased predation.
drought affects tree-hole mosquitoes in a manner that is predictable, and that the effects of drought on tree-hole mosquitoes are mediated by the physical and chemical characteristics of tree holes.
tree holes are not a homogeneous habitat and the physical and chemical attributes that define them can predict which mosquitoes are likely to be present and which are likely to survive.
